title: At an Old Service Station
description: Recall a traditional roadside service station through its pumps, tire equipment, and small automobile supplies.
cardDescription: Recall a traditional roadside service station through its pumps, tire equipment, and small automobile supplies.
focus: The scene combines refueling with the simple service items associated with older stations. A measuring display, a flexible delivery tube, and a vehicle fluid have different names.
solvingTip: Match the function first: delivering fuel, checking pressure, or clearing the windshield.
words: Hand-held fitting at the end of a gasoline delivery hose
Instrument used to check pressure inside a tire
Rubber-edged tool used to wipe liquid from windshield glass
United States liquid unit used in gasoline sales
Flexible tube linking a gasoline dispenser and its hand fitting
Lubricating liquid sold for a vehicle's engine
Gas supplied to inflate a vehicle's tires
Rubber covering around a vehicle wheel
Roadside display identifying the station or its prices
Paper road guide once offered at many stations
Cloth used to wipe oily hands or tools
Portable container used to carry an approved quantity of fuel
Work space in which a station mechanic services a car

answerNotes.NOZZLE: The nozzle directs fuel into the vehicle; the hose is the flexible connection to the pump.
answerNotes.PUMP: A fuel pump dispenses liquid and records an amount; it differs from a vehicle's internal engine pump.
answerNotes.GAUGE: A pressure gauge gives a measurement, while the inflation equipment supplies air.
answerNotes.SQUEEGEE: A squeegee removes liquid with a flexible edge rather than absorbing it like a towel.
answerNotes.GALLON: The US liquid gallon is the relevant unit at an American fuel station; the imperial gallon is a different volume.

title: A Roadside Motel Stop
description: Explore a traditional motor-court stay through its office, parking area, room fittings, and vacancy sign.
cardDescription: Explore a traditional motor-court stay through its office, parking area, room fittings, and vacancy sign.
focus: The motel scene emphasizes roadside arrangements such as parking near rooms and checking in at an office. The clues identify the accommodation, its availability, and ordinary room objects.
solvingTip: Separate a status shown on a sign from a room object or a place within the property.
words: Roadside lodging traditionally arranged for travelers arriving by car
Word on a lodging sign indicating an available room
Room where a motor-court guest traditionally checks in
Open-sided roofed shelter for a parked vehicle
Small object traditionally used to unlock a motel room
Glowing gas-discharge lighting associated with older motel signs
Private sleeping accommodation rented for a night
Space set aside for guests' vehicles
Furniture on which a motel guest sleeps
Room light placed beside a bed
Absorbent cloth provided in a guest bathroom
Frozen water obtained from a machine or bucket
Roadside display showing the motel's name
Price charged for a room over a stated period

answerNotes.MOTEL: Motel combines motor and hotel historically, but modern properties can have many different layouts.
answerNotes.VACANCY: Vacancy describes availability; it is not the name of a specific room type.
answerNotes.OFFICE: An office handles the arrival transaction, while the guest room provides the accommodation.
answerNotes.CARPORT: A carport provides a roof without the full enclosure of a conventional garage.
answerNotes.KEY: A physical key is one older arrangement; many properties now use cards or other access systems.

title: At the Soda Fountain
description: Visit a traditional soda fountain through its counter equipment, fizzy drinks, and ice-cream combinations.
cardDescription: Visit a traditional soda fountain through its counter equipment, fizzy drinks, and ice-cream combinations.
focus: The clues distinguish a soft-drink ingredient from a drink made with ice cream. Several familiar words name a serving container or a mixing action rather than a flavor.
solvingTip: Identify whether the clue asks for a beverage, an ingredient, or the vessel used to serve it.
words: Drink made by adding ice cream to a soft drink
Milkshake-style drink traditionally flavored with malted milk powder
Concentrated sweet liquid mixed into a fountain drink
Pressurized bottle used to dispense carbonated water
Soda ___, traditional name for a fountain-counter worker
Carbonated soft drink served at a fountain
Rounded portion of ice cream added to a drink
Narrow tube used to sip a tall fountain drink
Transparent vessel holding a fountain beverage
Bubbly layer forming on top of a fizzy drink
Small red fruit used as a sundae garnish
To combine drink ingredients until evenly mixed
Bubbling caused by escaping gas in a soft drink
Long serving surface at an old-fashioned soda fountain

answerNotes.FLOAT: A float combines ice cream and a beverage, commonly root beer; it differs from a fully blended shake.
answerNotes.MALT: Malt names a drink in this scene; the powder provides the characteristic flavor.
answerNotes.SYRUP: Syrup supplies sweetness and flavor, while carbonated water supplies the fizz.
answerNotes.SIPHON: A soda siphon dispenses fizzy water; its name is different from the ordinary open drinking glass.
answerNotes.JERK: The historical job name refers to operating fountain handles; the word has other meanings outside this phrase.

title: Through the Car Wash
description: Recognize the equipment and stages visible along an automatic car-wash lane.
cardDescription: Recognize the equipment and stages visible along an automatic car-wash lane.
focus: The scene names cleaning materials and machinery without prescribing a maintenance routine. A rotating brush, a spray fitting, and a drying air stream perform different jobs.
solvingTip: Look for what moves, what sprays, or what carries the vehicle through the lane.
words: Moving mechanism carrying a vehicle through some automatic washes
Machine directing strong air to help dry a washed vehicle
Cleaning agent mixed with water at a car wash
Small outlet directing a car-wash spray
Wash stage that carries loosened soap away with water
Bristled or soft-strip rotating cleaning tool
Common everyday name for the foaming wash product
Mass of bubbles covering a vehicle during washing
Protective finishing treatment offered by some car washes
Guided path followed by a vehicle's wheels
Covered passage containing a line of washing equipment
Fine directed stream of water from a cleaning fitting
To remove remaining water from a cleaned surface
Marked vehicle route toward the wash entrance

answerNotes.CONVEYOR: A conveyor moves the vehicle through certain wash designs; other systems move equipment around a stationary vehicle.
answerNotes.BLOWER: A blower moves air rather than wiping the surface with cloth.
answerNotes.DETERGENT: Detergent helps loosen soil; it is different from a wax treatment or plain rinsing water.
answerNotes.NOZZLE: A nozzle controls the spray pattern; the pump supplying pressure is a separate component.
answerNotes.RINSE: Rinsing removes washing solution; drying removes remaining surface water afterward.

title: A Glowing Roadside Sign
description: Explore the colors, shapes, and parts of a traditional illuminated sign through glass tubing and its supporting frame.
cardDescription: Explore the colors, shapes, and parts of a traditional illuminated sign through glass tubing and its supporting frame.
focus: Traditional neon signs produce light inside gas-filled tubes. Other gases, coatings, and modern lighting systems can produce different colors and effects, so neon is not a description of every luminous sign.
solvingTip: Use a physical part or a shape as a starting point before the lighting terms.
words: Gas producing a characteristic reddish-orange glow in a discharge tube
Hollow glass form bent into an illuminated sign's letters
Electrical contact at an end of a gas-discharge sign tube
Gas used in many discharge signs, often with other materials
Line tracing the outside shape of an illuminated letter
Transparent material shaped into a traditional sign tube
Steady visible light from an illuminated sign
Supporting structure behind a roadside display
Pointed sign shape directing attention toward an entrance
One alphabet character formed in bent tubing
Visual hue distinguishing one glowing section from another
Rounded bend in the shape of a sign
Dark time when a glowing roadside display stands out
Public display naming or advertising a roadside business

answerNotes.NEON: Neon gives its own characteristic color; signs in other colors may use different gases or fluorescent coatings.
answerNotes.TUBE: A sign tube holds the gas and follows a shaped outline; it is separate from the supporting frame.
answerNotes.ELECTRODE: Electrodes connect the electrical supply to the discharge; they are components rather than decorative letters.
answerNotes.ARGON: Argon is another sign-making gas; the broad everyday phrase neon sign can include arrangements that do not use neon alone.
answerNotes.OUTLINE: An outline follows a boundary rather than filling an entire shape with a solid surface.
